title: Potassium nitrite/epoxy based solid rocket propellant formulation development
author: Daniel Bontorin de Souza
abstract: This work was made whit the intent to improve the manufacturing process and the formulation of the solid propel- lant used in the rockets made by ITA Rocket Design. ITA Rocket Design is a group compose by undergraduate students from ITA that make model rockets to compete in national (Brazil) and international competitions. The program was kicked o? in August 2011 and every year the design is altered for improvements. This work shows the solid propellant preparation from easily available raw ingredients. The solid propellants ingredients are potassium nitrate and sorbitol, but it was also tested a new formulation using epoxy resin and aluminium powder. The ?rst step is to purify the potassium nitrate, then it gets mixed with melted sugar (and the other ingredients cited above for the new formulation). The propellant was putted to the test with small and real scale tests that allowed the evaluation of its performance as well as the solid motors performances. In the solid propellant manufacturing process, one of the most important steps is the casting that consists in pouring the propellant in its more ?uid state in a mold and then leaving it to cure or solidify. This step is very important because, if done wrong, could yield a propellant grain that contain lots of discontinuities such as voids and cracks and these could lead to a motor explosion. In a previous casting method, the propellant was subjected to a stress of compression, but for candy propellants, that have a crystalline characteristic, this stress due to compression increase the chances of a crack in the grain. Thus, is necessary to change the casting process and the new process developed is described in this work. Having reached a satisfactory line of production for the propellant, from the raw materials to the molded solid grain, it was time to review the formulation used to achieve better performances out of the propellant. And with a new formulation, it was conducted a thermochemical analysis to compare the old and new formulations.
